notes.summary: This chapter covers electric current, drift velocity, mobility and current density, Ohm's law and resistivity (including its temperature dependence), electrical energy and power, emf and internal resistance of a cell, combinations of cells, Kirchhoff's rules and the Wheatstone bridge. CBSE tests short numericals on drift velocity, resistance, cells and power along with conceptual and assertion-reason questions on resistivity and Kirchhoff's rules.
keyPoints: Current I = neAv_d; current density j = I/A = nev_d = σE. Drift speeds are tiny: n = 10²⁹ m⁻³, A = 1 mm², I = 1.6 A gives v_d = 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹.
Drift velocity v_d = eEτ/m; mobility μ = v_d/E = eτ/m, SI unit m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
Ohm's law V = IR and R = ρl/A. Resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ) depends on the material and temperature only, not on length or area. Stretching a wire to n times its length (volume constant) gives R' = n²R.

Metals: ρ_T = ρ₀[1 + α(T − T₀)]; ρ rises with temperature because the relaxation time τ falls. Semiconductors: ρ falls with temperature because the carrier density n rises sharply. Alloys such as nichrome, manganin and constantan have a very small α.
Power P = VI = I²R = V²/R; energy W = Pt, and 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. In series, the bulb of higher resistance (lower wattage rating) glows brighter; in parallel, the higher-rated bulb glows brighter.
Cell: while discharging V = E − Ir; while charging V = E + Ir; current I = E/(R + r). n identical cells in series: emf nE, internal resistance nr; in parallel: emf E, internal resistance r/n.
Two cells in parallel: E_eq = (E₁r₂ + E₂r₁)/(r₁ + r₂) and r_eq = r₁r₂/(r₁ + r₂). Cells in series with opposing polarity: net emf = E₁ − E₂.
Kirchhoff's junction rule (ΣI = 0 at a junction) follows from conservation of charge; the loop rule (ΣΔV = 0 around any closed loop) follows from conservation of energy.
A Wheatstone bridge is balanced when P/Q = R/S; then no current flows through the galvanometer, and that branch can be ignored when finding the equivalent resistance.
traps: Believing resistivity changes when a wire is cut, stretched or thickened — resistance changes, resistivity does not.
Using V = E − Ir for a battery that is being charged; during charging V = E + Ir.
Adding the emfs of cells joined with opposite polarity instead of subtracting them.
Assuming the higher-wattage bulb is always brighter — in series the lower-wattage, higher-resistance bulb is brighter.
Forgetting that 1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m² in drift velocity and resistance calculations.
notes.examTip: Before applying Kirchhoff's rules, mark a current direction in every branch and a sign for every cell and resistor; a negative answer only means the actual current flows the other way.

questions.text: Mobility of charge carriers is defined as the drift velocity per unit electric field. Its SI unit is
questions.explanation:
Mobility μ = v_d/E.
Unit = (m s⁻¹)/(V m⁻¹) = m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.text: A copper wire of cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m² carries a current of 1.6 A. If the number density of free electrons in copper is 1.0 × 10²⁹ m⁻³, the drift speed of the electrons is (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)
questions.explanation:
I = neAv_d, so v_d = I/(neA).
neA = 1.0 × 10²⁹ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ = 1.6 × 10⁴ C m⁻¹.
v_d = 1.6 / (1.6 × 10⁴) = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹, i.e. about 0.1 mm per second.

questions.text: A metal wire of resistance R is stretched uniformly until its length is doubled. Assuming its volume and resistivity remain unchanged, its new resistance is
questions.explanation:
With volume constant, doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area.
R = ρl/A, so R' = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A.
New resistance = 4R.

questions.text: The resistance of a metal wire is 10 Ω at 20 °C and 12 Ω at 120 °C. Taking 20 °C as the reference temperature, its temperature coefficient of resistance is
questions.explanation:
R_T = R₀[1 + α(T − T₀)], so α = (R_T − R₀)/[R₀(T − T₀)].
α = (12 − 10)/(10 × 100) = 2/1000.
α = 2 × 10⁻³ °C⁻¹.
Dividing by 12 Ω instead of the reference value 10 Ω gives the wrong value 1.67 × 10⁻³ °C⁻¹.

questions.text: A storage battery of emf 12 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is being charged by an external source with a current of 2 A. The potential difference across the terminals of the battery during charging is
questions.explanation:
During charging, current is driven into the battery at its positive terminal, so the terminal voltage must exceed the emf by the drop across the internal resistance.
V = E + Ir = 12 + 2 × 0.5.
V = 13 V. The value 11 V (E − Ir) applies only when the battery is discharging.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): If the length of a metal wire is doubled at the same temperature, its resistivity also doubles.
Reason (R): The resistance of a wire of uniform cross-section is directly proportional to its length.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ) depends only on the material and temperature, not on the dimensions, so A is false.
R = ρl/A shows that resistance is proportional to length, so R is true.
Hence A is false but R is true.

questions.text: Two cells of emf 6 V and 2 V, each of internal resistance 1 Ω, are connected in series with opposing polarity (positive terminal joined to positive terminal), and the combination is connected across an external resistor of 2 Ω. The current in the circuit is
questions.explanation:
By Kirchhoff's loop rule the opposing emfs subtract: net emf = 6 − 2 = 4 V.
Total resistance in the loop = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 Ω.
I = 4/4 = 1 A, in the direction driven by the 6 V cell.
Adding the emfs by mistake gives 8/4 = 2 A.

questions.text: With an increase in temperature, the resistivity of a semiconductor such as silicon decreases. The main reason is that
options: the relaxation time of the charge carriers increases
the number density of charge carriers increases
the mass of the charge carriers decreases
the vibrations of the lattice ions decrease
questions.explanation:
Resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ).
In a semiconductor, raising the temperature frees many more charge carriers, so n increases sharply.
This outweighs the fall in relaxation time τ (which gets shorter as lattice vibrations increase), so ρ decreases.

questions.text: Two electric bulbs rated 100 W, 220 V and 60 W, 220 V are connected in series across a 220 V supply. Which statement is correct?
options: The 100 W bulb glows brighter because it has the higher power rating.
Both bulbs glow equally because the same current flows through them.
The 60 W bulb glows brighter because it has the higher resistance and the same current flows through both.
The 60 W bulb glows brighter because a larger current flows through it.
questions.explanation:
R = V²/P: R(100 W) = 220²/100 = 484 Ω; R(60 W) = 220²/60 ≈ 807 Ω.
In series the current is the same: I = 220/(484 + 807) ≈ 0.17 A.
P = I²R is larger for the larger resistance: about 23.4 W in the 60 W bulb against 14.1 W in the 100 W bulb.
So the 60 W bulb glows brighter.

questions.text: Two cells, one of emf 6 V and internal resistance 1 Ω and the other of emf 3 V and internal resistance 2 Ω, are connected in parallel with like terminals joined together. The equivalent emf and equivalent internal resistance of the combination are
questions.explanation:
For two cells in parallel: E_eq = (E₁r₂ + E₂r₁)/(r₁ + r₂) and r_eq = r₁r₂/(r₁ + r₂).
E_eq = (6 × 2 + 3 × 1)/(1 + 2) = 15/3 = 5 V.
r_eq = (1 × 2)/(1 + 2) = 2/3 Ω ≈ 0.67 Ω.
Check: the circulating current (6 − 3)/(1 + 2) = 1 A gives a terminal voltage of 6 − 1 × 1 = 5 V.

questions.text: In a Wheatstone bridge ABCD, P = 2 Ω is connected between A and B, Q = 4 Ω between B and C, R = 3 Ω between A and D, and S = 6 Ω between D and C. A galvanometer of resistance 10 Ω is connected between B and D. The equivalent resistance between A and C is
questions.explanation:
P/Q = 2/4 = 1/2 and R/S = 3/6 = 1/2, so the bridge is balanced and no current flows through the galvanometer.
The galvanometer branch can be ignored: arm ABC = 2 + 4 = 6 Ω and arm ADC = 3 + 6 = 9 Ω, in parallel.
R_eq = (6 × 9)/(6 + 9) = 54/15 = 3.6 Ω.
